item.title: A Drone Killed Three Ukrainians. It Was Guided Entirely by A.I.
item.description: An attack by what Ukrainian officials said was a Russian drone with an Nvidia chip presages a dystopian future of weaponry untethered to humans.
item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer and Nicole Tung
item.media:credit: Nicole Tung for The New York Times

item.title: Some of Russia’s A.I. Drones Are Powered by Nvidia Microcomputers, Ukrainian Officials Say
item.description: The tech giant says it does not sell the devices in Russia, but they are widely available on resale markets. When purchased that way, they are virtually impossible to track.
item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer
item.media:credit: Nicole Tung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Nvidia Jetson Orin minicomputer that Ukrainian officials say was found in an autonomous drone that Russia recently tested in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine.

item.title: UK Prime Minister Burnham Arrives in Ukraine as Russia Amps Up Warnings
item.description: In his first foreign trip since taking office, Prime Minister Andy Burnham affirmed support for Kyiv despite new warnings from Moscow of potential consequences.
item.dc:creator: Michael D. Shear
item.media:description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham of Britain on Monday at the tomb of the unknown soldier at Ukraine’s national military memorial cemetery in Hatne, southwest of Kyiv.

item.title: Canada Is ‘at War’ With U.S. Over Tariffs, and U.S.P.S. Publishes Plan to Restrict Ballots
item.description: Plus, what it’s like to live next to a roller coaster.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Mumford, Will Jarvis, Margaret Kadifa, Jake Lucas and Ian Stewart
item.media:description: In a speech on Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said the country was under attack by President Trump’s tariffs and “at war” with the United States.

item.title: U.S. to Unveil ‘Economic D-Day’ Sanctions Targeting Iran’s Economy

item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said last week that countries that continue to do business with Iran would face the “full might and force” of the U.S. government.

item.title: Iran Cracks Down on One Luxury Left to Its Youth: Coffee Shops
item.description: In recent weeks, the police have closed dozens of cafes, often citing laws that stipulate women must veil in public. Experts say the closures are part of an effort to control public space.

item.media:description: Iranians at a cafe in Tehran in April.

item.title: Farmers Struggle to Get Basic Services From Depleted Agriculture Dept.
item.description: After the departure of thousands of federal workers, rural communities report problems obtaining loans, grants, technical assistance and support for infrastructure and other services.
item.dc:creator: Linda Qiu
item.media:credit: Nina Riggio for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mary and Zachariah Ben turned to private lenders when the low-interest loan they secured from the administration to buy property for their organic baby food business stalled for months.

item.title: In West Texas, Trump’s Border Wall Collides With Latino History
item.description: A century ago, Mexican American families came together to build an adobe church near the border. Can its bell toll again as the wall expansion nears?
item.dc:creator: Jazmine Ulloa and Paul Ratje
item.media:description: The Friends of the Ruidosa Church group has worked to restore the adobe mission for the last 20 years. Members of the group worry that border wall construction could damage the site.

item.title: U.S. Military Kills 2 People in Attack on Boat in Pacific
item.description: The United States has killed at least 223 people since its campaign of boat strikes began nearly a year ago.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: A screen grab from a video posted by U.S. Southern Command on Monday showed what it said was a vessel operating along a drug-trafficking route in the Eastern Pacific.

item.title: Can Democrats Win Back the Senate? Why Their Chances Are Improving.

item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Christopher Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: James Talarico, a Democrat, is trying win a Senate race in Texas after decades of disappointments for his party.

item.title: As Democrats Struggle in Some Western States, Independents See an Opening
item.description: From South Dakota to Alaska, independents are challenging incumbent Republicans and eschewing a Democratic label that Western voters find toxic.

item.media:description: Todd Achilles is among a wave of independent challengers.

item.title: California Cancels Talks With Paramount Over Warner Bros. Merger
item.description: The attorney general of California, one of 12 states suing to block the $111 billion deal, accused Paramount of leaking and misrepresenting earlier settlement discussions.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:description: California’s attorney general, Rob Bonta, announced last month that he and 11 other state attorneys general would sue to block Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

item.title: The Ruthless Efficiency of Ultrapotent Street Drugs
item.description: Five decades after the “war on drugs” sought to make substance abuse unaffordable, illicit drugs are cheaper and more powerful than ever. A visit to Baltimore shows why.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel
item.media:credit: KT Kanazawich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last summer, the city of Baltimore experienced several mass overdose crises, the result of fentanyl being mixed with powerful synthetic chemicals.

item.title: Why Getting High Has Only Gotten Cheaper
item.description: The “war on drugs” sought to reduce substance abuse by driving up prices and lowering demand. Today, street drugs are less expensive and more dangerous than ever.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel and Irena Hwang

item.title: Washington Post Ordered to Rehire Fired Columnist Karen Attiah
item.description: An arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Karen Attiah, who was fired after posting about “white men who espouse hatred and violence” following Charlie Kirk’s killing.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:description: Karen Attiah in 2018. “This decision confirms what we’ve said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion writer, and this was wrongful termination,” she said.
